curriculum.title: Cambridge Primary Global Perspectives
curriculum.note: There is no Global Perspectives folder for this year group on Google Drive. The objectives below are taken verbatim from the Stages 5 and 6 column of the 0838 Primary Global Perspectives Progression Grid, which is in the Primary 1 folder and covers every stage. Cambridge sets one objective for Stages 5 and 6 together, so Primary 6 works towards the same objectives as Primary 5; the challenge topics here are deliberately different so the two years do not repeat, and the expectation is that Primary 6 meets them with more independence.

objectives.title: Identify some key points from different perspectives on the same issue within a source
Find and interpret simple patterns in graphical or numerical data
Talk about simple causes of a local issue and consequences on others
Suggest and justify an action to make a positive difference to a local issue
Work positively with team members, contributing useful ideas and helping to solve problems to improve team work or to achieve a shared outcome
The team plans and divides tasks fairly to achieve a shared outcome, considering the skills of team members and the time available, and manages disagreements
Present information clearly with an appropriate structure and with some reference to sources where appropriate
Listen to ideas and information about an issue and ask questions relevant to the issue
Discuss a source, considering the author or purpose, and use this to comment on its strengths and limitations
Discuss own opinion about another's perspective, identifying points you agree or disagree with
Discuss the impact of personal contribution on teamwork
Identify benefits and challenges of working together to achieve a shared outcome
Discuss ways that personal ideas may have been influenced by new information or the ideas of others
Identify skills learned or improved during an activity
Begin to construct research questions with support
Identify sources and locate relevant information and answers to questions within them
Conduct investigations, using interviews or questionnaires to test a prediction or begin to answer a research question
Select, organise and record relevant information from sources and findings from primary research, using an appropriate method

plan.prior: First lesson of this unit. Draw on what learners already know.
plan.next: Lesson 2: Constructing research questions about fairness
plan.intro: Read one short source together and ask who is speaking in it.
main: Model pulling out the key points of one perspective and marking them in the text.
Learners find a second perspective in the same source and mark it too.

objectives.title: The team plans and divides tasks fairly to achieve a shared outcome, considering the skills of team members and the time available, and manages disagreements
Work positively with team members, contributing useful ideas and helping to solve problems to improve team work or to achieve a shared outcome

plan.focus: Planning and dividing the tasks fairly
plan.prior: Lesson 5: Selecting, organising and recording our information
plan.next: Lesson 7: Presenting clearly, and the impact of what I contributed
plan.intro: Name the shared outcome and the time we have. Both, before anything else.
main: Teams list every task the outcome needs, then estimate how long each will take.
Teams divide the tasks by what each member is good at, and write it down.
Teams agree in advance how they will settle a disagreement.
Teams work, and record any change they had to make to the plan.
plan.plenary: Each team reports whether the plan survived contact with the work.
plan.look_for: A fair division based on skills and time, and disagreements handled, not avoided.
